grades.quote: The SIE bit enables or disables all interrupts in supervisor mode. When SIE is clear, interrupts are not taken while in supervisor mode. When the hart is running in user-mode, the value in SIE is ignored, and supervisor-level interrupts are enabled.
grades.reason: Explains a concrete user-versus-supervisor execution difference and privilege transitions, but not the general purpose of privilege levels.

grades.quote: When V=1, the hart is either in virtual S-mode (VS-mode), or in virtual U-mode (VU-mode) atop a guest OS running in VS-mode. When V=0, the hart is either in M-mode, in HS-mode, or in U-mode atop an OS running in HS-mode.
grades.reason: Directly identifies execution modes, explains their host/guest roles, and supplies their privilege hierarchy and translation differences.

grades.quote: The SUM (permit Supervisor User Memory access) bit modifies the privilege with which S-mode loads and stores access virtual memory. When SUM=0, S-mode memory accesses to pages that are accessible by U-mode (U=1 in Figure 67) will fault. When SUM=1, these accesses are permitted. SUM has no effect when page-based virtual memory is not in effect, nor when executing in U-mode. Note that S-mode can never execute instructions from user pages, regardless of the state of SUM.
grades.reason: Provides substantive memory-access distinctions and protection rationale, but only one aspect of execution privilege.

grades.quote: As shown in Figure 7.8(c), this allows the outgoing thread, the scheduler, and the incoming thread to all execute in user mode with no mode switch—provided the two threads are in the same process.
grades.reason: Offers auxiliary context about user-level scheduling and avoiding mode switches, without explaining privilege levels or their protections.
